title: Rebuild-on-publish: Amplify StartJob / Pretext revalidation from publish, staging rebuild on demand
description:
## Goal
Publishing makes the public site update without a human: after `publishItem`/`papyrus content publish`, (a) Pretext sites revalidate the affected pages immediately, (b) Markus-static sites start a rebuild of the reader app. The staging site's static preview can be rebuilt on demand from the newsroom ("Preview"). No webhook URL and no token: the trigger is an IAM-authorized `amplify:StartJob` call from the backend Lambda (decision: Amplify build-webhook URLs are bearer secrets; Ryan's rule is no long-lived tokens).

## Context (verified)
- Pretext revalidation exists: `app/api/revalidate/route.ts` (POST, header `x-papyrus-revalidate-secret` == `PAPYRUS_REVALIDATE_SECRET`; body `{ editionDate?, articleSlugs?, itemSlugs?, paths?, tags? }`; revalidates `articleCacheTag(slug)`, `/articles/<slug>`, edition tags) and its Python caller `src/papyrus_content/reader_revalidation.py` `trigger_reader_cache_revalidation(edition_date, article_slugs, item_slugs)` (base URL/secret from `papyrus_config.resolve_reader_revalidation_base_url/resolve_reader_cache_revalidate_secret`; returns `None` when unset; used by `seed_edition_content`). `editionDate` is `str` there, but the route treats it as optional.
- No Amplify trigger exists. Amplify Hosting has no CloudFormation resource for webhooks (webhooks are created via `create-webhook` and yield a secret URL), but `amplify:StartJob` (`jobType RELEASE`, app id + branch) is a normal IAM action. `PPY-39f928` creates the reader app (`WEB`, branch `main`) and outputs its id.
- `PPY-3e5235` adds the Lambda `papyrus-content-actions` whose handler calls `papyrus_content.publishing.publish_item`; `amplify/site-backend-config.ts` `PapyrusSiteBackendConfig` is the per-site config object.

## Exact changes
1. `amplify/site-backend-config.ts`: add `reader?: { amplifyAppId: string; branchName?: string }` (static reader app to rebuild) and `stagingBuild?: { enabled: boolean }` (lets the newsroom start the staging branch build of this CMS app).
2. `amplify/site-backend.ts`: pass to the `contentActions` Lambda env `PAPYRUS_READER_AMPLIFY_APP_ID`, `PAPYRUS_READER_BRANCH` (default `main`), `PAPYRUS_CMS_AMPLIFY_APP_ID` (this app: `AWS_APP_ID` at synth), `PAPYRUS_STAGING_BRANCH` (`staging`), `PAPYRUS_REVALIDATE_BASE_URL` and secret via the existing Amplify `secret("PAPYRUS_REVALIDATE_SECRET")` pattern used for other Python Lambdas (L629-639); add `lambda.addToRolePolicy(new PolicyStatement({ actions: ["amplify:StartJob", "amplify:ListJobs"], resources: [arn:aws:amplify:<region>:<account>:apps/<readerAppId>/branches/*, arn:aws:amplify:...:apps/<cmsAppId>/branches/staging/*] }))` (only the ids that are configured).
3. `src/papyrus_content/rebuild_trigger.py` (new):
   ```python
   def trigger_rebuild(*, reader_app_id: str | None, reader_branch: str = "main", boto_client=None) -> dict
   def trigger_staging_build(*, cms_app_id: str, staging_branch: str = "staging", boto_client=None) -> dict
   def trigger_pretext_revalidation(slugs: list[str], edition_date: str | None) -> dict | None   # wraps reader_revalidation
   ```
   `trigger_rebuild`: `amplify.list_jobs(appId, branchName, maxResults=5)`; if a job with status `PENDING` exists, skip (it has not started, so it will export the content including this publish); otherwise `start_job(jobType="RELEASE")` (a `RUNNING` job does not block a new one: Amplify queues it, and the new job sees this publish). Returns `{"started": bool, "jobId": ..., "reason": ...}`. boto3 is in the Lambda runtime.
4. `papyrus_content/publishing.py` (`PPY-b3a10e`): no change. In the Lambda handler (`amplify/functions/content-actions/handler.py`) after a successful, changed `publishItem`/`unpublishItem`: call `trigger_pretext_revalidation([slug], edition_date)` when `PAPYRUS_REVALIDATE_BASE_URL` is set and `trigger_rebuild(...)` when `PAPYRUS_READER_AMPLIFY_APP_ID` is set; failures are caught and returned as `{"rebuild": {"started": false, "error": "..."}}` in the response (a publish never fails because the trigger failed; the response tells the editor). New GraphQL mutation `requestStagingBuild` (same Lambda, `PPY-3e5235` file list: `schema.ts` + `resource.ts`) calling `trigger_staging_build`.
5. CLI: `papyrus content publish` (from `PPY-b3a10e`) calls `trigger_pretext_revalidation` (existing env config) and, when `--rebuild-app-id <id>` (or env `PAPYRUS_READER_AMPLIFY_APP_ID`) is given, `trigger_rebuild` using the caller's AWS credentials (OIDC role from `PPY-e7f81e` in CI). `--no-trigger` skips both. Add `papyrus content rebuild --reader | --staging --app-id <id>` for manual use.
6. UI (`PPY-8ef4ca` component, small follow-up here): after Publish show "Site rebuild started" / "Live site updates within a few minutes" from the response, and a `Preview` button (only when the static staging flag `NEXT_PUBLIC_PAPYRUS_STAGING_BUILD=1` is set) calling `requestStagingBuild`.

## Data shapes
`publishItem` response gains `"rebuild": {"started": true, "jobId": "42"}` or `{"started": false, "reason": "pending-job-exists"}` and `"revalidated": {"ok": true}`. IAM statement: `Action: ["amplify:StartJob","amplify:ListJobs"]`, `Resource: ["arn:aws:amplify:us-east-1:335163751677:apps/<readerAppId>/branches/main/jobs/*", ...]` (use the exact resource ARN form the Amplify API requires; verify with `aws amplify start-job --debug` in a sandbox account and fix the pattern).

## Tests
- Unit `procedures/newsroom/tests/test_rebuild_trigger.py` with a stub boto client: starts a job when none pending; skips when `PENDING` exists; returns `started False` with the error message when `start_job` raises (never raises); `trigger_pretext_revalidation` returns `None` when unconfigured.
- Handler test (extends `test_content_actions_handler.py` from `PPY-3e5235`): a changed publish returns `rebuild.started True` (stub); an unchanged publish returns no trigger; a trigger failure leaves `ok: true`.
- Gherkin (behave): `features_backend/rebuild-on-publish.feature`: "Publishing starts a reader rebuild", "Publishing while a build is pending does not queue another", "A failed trigger does not fail the publish".
- Sandbox with a scratch Amplify reader app (Ryan connects it, or use any WEB app): publish an item, `aws amplify list-jobs --app-id <id> --branch-name main` shows a new job.

## Acceptance checks
- `poetry run python -m unittest procedures.newsroom.tests.test_rebuild_trigger procedures.newsroom.tests.test_content_actions_handler -v`, `poetry run behave features_backend/rebuild-on-publish.feature`, `npx tsc --noEmit` pass.
- `node scripts/test-infra-synth.mjs` (from `PPY-39f928`) still passes and the content-actions role policy contains only the two Amplify actions on the configured apps (add an assertion by synthesizing the backend with a `reader` config, using the existing site-backend test harness or a `cdk`-free snapshot of the policy builder function).
- Sandbox job check above.

## Dependencies
Blocked by `PPY-3e5235` (handler), `PPY-b3a10e`, `PPY-39f928` (reader app id as config), `PPY-f00c89` (staging build contract for `requestStagingBuild`). Same-file conflicts: `amplify/site-backend.ts`, `amplify/site-backend-config.ts`, `amplify/data/schema.ts`/`resource.ts` (with `PPY-3e5235`).

## Risks
- Build storms: a bulk import publishing 200 items starts at most one pending job (the pending-job rule); the importer (`PPY-22a3b4`) should call `trigger_rebuild` once at the end (add that call in `markus_import_commands.py` behind `--rebuild-app-id`), not per item.
- Amplify `StartJob` on a branch that is not connected to a repo (Anth.us today is manual zip) fails; `reason` is returned and surfaced; it works after the GitHub App connection.
- The two triggers differ for Pretext (cache tags) and static (full rebuild); a site sets only the one that applies.

## Needs Ryan
The reader app must be connected through the GitHub App first (`PPY-39f928`); otherwise nothing to rebuild.

## Common rules (apply to every Phase 2 ticket)
- Work from a clean worktree of `origin/develop` (`git -C /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus fetch origin && git worktree add ../Papyrus-worktrees/<this-ticket> -b feature/PPY-fbb1fb-<slug> origin/develop`). Never commit to `develop` or `main`; open a PR into `develop`; never merge to `main`. Conventional-commit messages. Update this ticket with branch, PR link and the verification output.
- `AGENTS.md` rules that bind this work: no backward-compatibility shims or fallbacks (clean breaks); backend tooling in Python unless noted; Pretext owns text measurement (do not measure DOM in React); read `AGENTS.local.md` before ANY AWS/Amplify/sandbox command; never run `ampx pipeline-deploy` locally (sandbox only).
- Note on language direction: Ryan's 2026-10-05 correction (epic comment 4174c5) says Papyrus is being ported from Python to TypeScript. Phase 2 follows the approved design in docs/standard-site.md (Python CLI/Lambdas + `papyrus-newsroom`). Keep new Python logic in small pure functions with fixture-driven tests so it can be ported; do not add new Python dependencies beyond those named here.
- Tests: Python unit tests are `unittest` under `procedures/newsroom/tests/` (run: `poetry run python -m unittest procedures.newsroom.tests.<module> -v`); backend Gherkin is `behave` under `features_backend/` with steps in `features_backend/steps/` (run: `poetry run behave features_backend/<file>.feature`); UI Gherkin is cucumber-js + Playwright under `features/` (run against a dev server: `npm run dev` then `PAPYRUS_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3001 npx cucumber-js features/<file>.feature`); TypeScript unit tests are `scripts/test-*.ts` run with `npx tsx` (add an npm script `test:<name>` in package.json).
- Install: `poetry install --extras "newsroom markus"` and `npm ci`. Verify `markus --version` prints 0.5.1 (PyPI `anthus-markus` 0.5.1 emits IR `schema_version: 1`).
right_now_summary: Publishing now triggers page revalidation or a reader rebuild, while staging previews can be rebuilt on demand.
